title: Ramp Help Center
snippet:
Ramp’s Developer API allows teams to programmatically access Ramp data and build automations or integrations tailored to their workflows. It provides secure, scoped access to objects like transactions, cards, users, and more.

To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.
Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead. See Publish an app for other Ramp businesses.
1. Open [Developer apps](https://app.ramp.com/settings/ramp-developer/apps) in Ramp.
2. For your first app, click **Start building**. If you already have an app, click **Create new app**.
3. Name your app (e.g., “API Quickstart”) and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types**, confirm **Client credentials** is turned on.
5. Under **Scopes**, click **Configure allowed scopes** and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as `transactions:read`. If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access.
6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securely—you’ll need them to generate your access token.

title: API Agreement
snippet:
“Ramp APIs” means (i) any software, code, services, accounts, keys, or information related to Ramp’s application programming interface, including the developer console and all other tools, elements, components and executables, (ii) any Ramp-provided or Ramp-authorized protocol, server, connector, or interface that enables programmatic or automated access to Customer Data or Services, including any model context protocol (“MCP”) server, command line interface, agent tool interface, or similar technology, whether existing now or developed in the future, and (iii) documentation that Ramp makes available to help enable use.

- **2.1****API Access**. To receive access to the Ramp APIs in a sandbox or production environment, you must submit a request for Ramp review. Ramp may approve, condition, limit, or deny any request for access in our sole discretion, and may suspend or revoke access to either at any time for any reason. Access credentials for a Developer Account are non-transferable, non-assignable, and must be kept confidential. All activity occurring under your credentials is your responsibility.

- **3.1****Use of Ramp APIs.** Subject to your compliance with all of the Developer Terms, Ramp grants you a limited, non-exclusive, non-assignable, non-transferable, revocable right to use the Ramp APIs solely to internally develop, test, and support an integration of your Application with the Services, and allow Customers to use your integration of the Ramp APIs within your Application. You may use the Ramp APIs only as expressly permitted in the Developer Terms. We provide no Services to you under the Developer Terms.

title: docs.ramp.com/llms-guides/getting-started.txt
snippet:
First, you'll need to create a developer app to get your API credentials.
1. In your Ramp account, go to **Company → Developer** (you'll need admin access).
2. Click **Create New App**.
3. Name your app (e.g., "API Quickstart") and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types**, click **Add new grant type** → select **Client Credentials**.
5. Under **Scopes**, click **Configure allowed scopes** and select `transactions:read`.
6. Copy your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.

With your credentials, request an access token. Ramp authenticates this `/developer/v1/token` request with HTTP Basic Auth: base64-encode `client_id:client_secret` and send it in the `Authorization` header. The token authenticates your API requests.

title: docs.ramp.com/llms-guides/authorization.txt
snippet:
## Supported grant types
| Grant Type | Use Case | User Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Client Credentials** | Internal integrations, server-to-server | None required |
| **Authorization Code** | Third-party apps, public integrations | Authorized user consent required |
| **Refresh Token** | Renew access after an Authorization Code grant | None after the initial authorization |

`cards:read_vault` is available only to approved integrators; see [Virtual Cards](</developer-api/v1/virtual-cards#vault-api>). Scopes marked partners only appear in the partner Developer Console, not in a business's own Developer API settings. Some endpoints also require a Ramp plan feature and return `403` without it, even with the right scope.
## Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI
[Ramp MCP](</developer-api/v1/ramp-mcp>) and [Ramp CLI](</developer-api/v1/cli>) don't use OAuth scopes to limit access. A connection can do what the connecting user's Ramp role allows, so new tools don't fail with missing-scope errors.

title: How to use Ramp API ?
snippet:
Developers access the Ramp API through a straightforward process involving account creation, key generation, and environment selection. Begin by signing up for a [Ramp business account ](https://ramp.com/?ref=apidog.com)if you lack one.

Ramp structures its API pricing around the broader platform fees, ensuring predictability for developers. The core Ramp service operates on a no-monthly-fee model for card issuance, but API usage ties into transaction volumes.
Basic access to the API comes free with any Ramp account. You incur no additional charges for standard endpoints like transactions or cards. However, advanced features—such as custom webhook processing or high-volume data exports—may require enterprise plans.
Ramp's pricing emphasizes per-transaction savings rather than API-specific fees. The platform offers 1.5% cashback on all card spends, with no foreign transaction fees. For API-driven automations, this translates to cost efficiencies: automate reconciliations to cut accounting hours by up to 80%.

Free tier supports unlimited projects—download now to complement your Ramp API setup.

title: Introducing Ramp’s Technology Partner Program
snippet:
In recent months, we have expanded the ways businesses and developers can build on Ramp. Our developer API continues to grow. Our recently refreshed API documentation makes it easier to understand what is available and get started. Partners can work with real-time spend data, approval workflows, user provisioning and spend controls, virtual cards, vendor payouts, and more.

Partnerships should get more valuable as the work compounds. The Ramp Technology Partner Program is designed to do that.
Partners are eligible to receive referral incentives and starts with access to the Partner Portal, aggregated client insights, a co-branded referral page, and Sandbox and Developer Console access. As partners grow, the program adds the support and investment needed to further build and go to market together.
